How one Star Wars actor became the CEO of Commodore
Peri Fractic on how Commodore is capitalizing on a growing desire to disconnect
Christopher Dring
11 hours ago
Listen now on Apple , Spotify or YouTube
In This Edition,
Commodore CEO Peri Fractic on…
The return of the C64
Its ‘digital detox’ flip phone
The Cyberpunk partnership
Getting to the level of Atari
Did you know that the CEO of Commodore was in Star Wars: Episode 1 – The Phantom Menace?
It was his first film role. He was seen running across a hangar while being shot at. And Christian Simpson, or Peri Fractic as he’s known, would appear in various Star Wars movies through the years.
How Fractic went from a galaxy far, far away to Commodore was via his YouTube channel. As a fan of retro, and owner of a Commodore 64 and Amstrad PCW, Fractic began doing retro videos. And then in 2024, he reviewed the Commodore 64X (a PC based on the original 1982 Commodore 64). That video clocked up over a million views and caught the eye of the Commodore brand owners.
Fractic, alongside fellow experts Leo Nigro and Sean Donohue, made three proposals to Commodore. The first was around working together, the second involved licensing the brand, and the third (suggested half-jokingly) was to buy the company.
They took the third option.
“You seem to know Commodore better than we do,” they told Fractic. “So we might like to sell you the whole company”.
The C64 returns
Under new ownership, Commodore released the Commodore 64 Ultimate last year, a system that replicated the original machine with a few enhancements.
However, Fractic is wary that retro hardware has a potentially limited lifespan.
“It is big in the sense that all those parents, even grandparents, are now introducing their kids to it,” Fractic tells us outside the company’s Gamescom booth.
“The nostalgia sort of permeates through two, three generations. You look [on our booth], there’s a kid playing on a C64 right now. Who’s next to him? His dad. That works really well for keeping nostalgia alive.
“But you look at it as a segment, it’s still small and hobbyist. Also, we’re not getting any younger. You could argue that that will eventually dwindle. But our goal is you attract Gen Z with the Y2K aesthetics. Those kids, instead of just saying, ‘That’s cool, Dad’, and then going back to their iPhones, they’re now going to see this surrounding them, and feel this is a vibe they like. And that way, it becomes sustainable. Those kids grow up, and they show their kids, and we keep doing this.
“But it could dwindle, which is why we have to do modern products alongside it.”
The digital detox
That ‘modern’ product is the Callback 8020, a flip phone that runs Android apps but blocks web browsers and social media.
“People want to go back to simpler tech. They’re getting sick of their data being harvested and sold, tracking everywhere, tracking cookies,” Fractic says. “People want to go back to a simpler tech. Commodore is from that time.
“The lights dimmed [on Commodore] in 1994, right before the internet became a thing. It almost makes sense if you reboot Commodore, you start where you left off. So, now we’re in the 1995 to 2000 era for Commodore. Which is perfect, because that’s what people want to go back to.
“That’s where digital minimalism fits in perfectly with Commodore.”
“We’re in the 1995 to 2000 era for Commodore. Which is perfect, because that’s what people want to go back to”
The Commodore 64 Ultimate was a hit. It generated $2 million in revenue in three weeks, with 27,000 units sold. “Which is mind-blowing for a 40-year-old computer,” Fractic noted.
However, the Callback 8020 did in one weekend what the C64 managed in three months.
“The movement is huge towards digital minimalism, more intentional tech,” Fractic explains. “You’ve seen people buying vinyl records again, going back to flip phones organically, and just getting off Facebook. It’s happening with or without us. But my philosophy is we need to build Commodore into the same level as Google and Apple. So, we can do the cool retro things for the fans. But… how do we build Commodore to be that big based on nostalgia alone? That’s a niche. You can’t do it as a hobbyist, boutique brand. So, our philosophy with the flip phone, and with other things you’re going to see from us, is those bring in the bigger audience.”
That includes its latest tie-in with CD Projekt Red. At Gamescom, Commodore showcased the Commodore 77, which is a version of the C64 based around the hit RPG Cyberpunk 2077.
“In Cyberpunk, their 2077 version of the future stems away from our real future in the early ‘80s. Some people say 1982 or ‘84, is when the Cyberpunk timeline diverges,” says Fractic. “In our story, Commodore survived, continued on, and in 2077, it’s still a brand that people love. So, in their world, you can still buy a 64, but it’s now a 77, it’s been upgraded a bit.
“Retro-futurism is how you describe Cyberpunk. Like Blade Runner. Our whole philosophy here is we do retro, and we do future. We do the two hand-in-hand.”
The component crisis
Unfortunately for the new-look Commodore, its comeback has coincided with the global component crisis, with the price of RAM and storage having a significant impact on hardware costs.
“We’ve been somewhat impacted, yes,” admits Fractic. “We’ve been quite lucky that we made a decision early on to buy up a bunch of FPGAs, more than we needed. There was talk of using them in a separate product, so we had them on standby. Then when the FPGA prices more than doubled, we were able to tap into our existing stock of 10,000 FPGAs. It does continue to impact us. We see a lot of complaints about the phone price. We found a way to drop it by $100, but $399 for a flip phone, although it’s not your granny’s flip phone, can seem expensive. That is purely because the RAM price went from $11 per unit to $86 per unit.
“That’s just for the memory. That’s before you look at development, software licensing, everything else. To release that phone for $400, we have a tiny sliver of a margin on that.”
The new Commodore isn’t all about hardware, however. It’s also investing in games. At the end of last year, it released Jupiter Lander 2: Jupiter Fracture for the C64 Ultimate, which is a sequel to the original 1982 game. And late last month it published the Alien Breed 35 th Anniversary Collection, in collaboration with developer Antstream and Alien Breed owners Team17, on consoles and PC.
“Alien Breed was something that was pitched to us by Antstream and Team17,” Fractic says. “They’d done a lot of the legwork already. We were able to come in and help with the publishing, and obviously it’s got our name front and center, which is amazing.
“We receive pitches almost daily. We just announced something called ‘Made for Ultimate’, which is to develop games specifically for the C64 Ultimate to take advantage of the extra 24 channels of sound, the extra RAM and CPU speed. If you go to the bottom of our website, there is something that says ‘Build with us.’ You can submit stuff. I look at every single submission personally.”
He adds that software is very much part of the future plan, but he’s wary of expanding too fast.
“Everything still passes across my desk, every single decision, because I want it to have one very clear vision,” he says. “There’s a reason in Hollywood you have one director on set, so the movie is one vision. We’re being very cautious about expansion. We have about 30 team members now, which almost feels too big for a startup. But when you look at the scale of what we’re doing, I couldn’t do it alone. We’re very slowly bringing on team members and being cautious with the cash flow.”
“I don’t know if we’ll become a public company, but we get a lot of requests for that from the fanbase”
Ultimately, the goal is to try and replicate some of the success seen by another iconic gaming brand that’s enjoyed quite the retro revival.
“I do see [us being at the level of] Atari in terms of the turnover they’re generating,” Fractic says of the five-year vision.
“They’re a public company. I don’t know if we’ll become a public company, but we get a lot of requests for that from the fanbase. They want to own a piece of Commodore. And that would be one of a couple of ways we could allow people to have a share certificate for Commodore on your wall.
“I originally said I want to do two things really well every year. We’ve done, I think, six or seven things. Every single one’s been successful. We’re very lucky. I’d like to still not do too much, and just keep growing.”

title: QuestMobile 2026年三季度AI应用市场发展报告：AI原生App用户5.46亿，三大入口收敛承接生活+办公交付，双主线驱动市场变局
author: QuestMobile
text:
QuestMobile数据显示，截止到2026年9月，AI综合助手用户规模达到11.57亿，同比增长44%。其中，AI生活助手用户规模达到3.47亿，同比增长55%；同时，AI办公月活规模已经达到1.42亿，同比增长50.6%，其中WorkBuddy、百度搭子、千问办公规模分别为3235.3万、977万、790.5万。

涉及行业：聚合信息、手机品牌、系统工具、办公商务

title: 2026年数字银行市场洞察
author: Sensor Tower
text:
数字银行已成为日常金融活动的重要组成部分，为消费者提供更加快捷、便利的账户管理、支付、转账及其他金融服务，同时帮助银行扩大服务覆盖范围并提升运营效率。随着数字银行日益普及，全球银行网站访问量有所下降，主要原因是桌面端流量减少；与此同时，移动网站端的访问量占比则已升至约 40%。即使通过浏览器访问银行服务，消费者也越来越多地使用移动设备。
这一向移动端迁移的趋势，也体现在银行应用的下载量增长与使用上。2026 年第一季度，移动银行持续增长，季度下载量保持在 5 亿次以上，同比增长 4%。用户参与度增长更快，总会话次数上升 10%，表明消费者不仅在大规模使用银行应用，在日常金融活动中的使用频率也不断提高。
在更广泛的金融服务应用类别中，截至 2026 年 5 月的 12 个月，银行应用仍是规模最大的细分品类， 累计下载量约为 23 亿次，同比增长 7% 。其他移动金融细分品类主要围绕特定金融需求发展，例如数字钱包用于支付、贷款应用满足信贷需求、投资应用助力财富增值；但银行应用仍是账户、存款、储蓄、转账及日常资金管理的基础。
尽管同比下降 2%， 拉丁美洲 仍是银行应用下载量最大的市场， 占全球总量的 21% 。在主要市场中，印度增长最为强劲，增幅达 17%；东南亚和欧洲也实现增长。这表明传统银行应用与数字优先型银行模式的普及程度均在提升，在大型移动优先经济体中尤其明显。
如需深入了解数字银行如何重塑全球金融服务格局，以及哪些市场、银行模式、用户参与度趋势和广告策略正在驱动行业下一阶段增长，请下载完整版《 2026年数字银行市场洞察 》。
注：本报告的下载量数据基于 App Store 和 Google Play 的预估值，不包括预装、重新下载及第三方 Android 应用商店的下载量。如需获取更多洞察，请点击下方按钮，免费查看完整报告。
下载免费报告
新型银行 与传统银行竞逐移动银行市场领导地位
随着消费者越来越多地通过应用管理个人财务，市场竞争正日益聚焦于两大银行模式。数字银行与新型银行凭借无网点、移动优先的服务模式进入市场；传统机构——包括老牌银行、旗下纯数字品牌，以及邮政银行、合作银行和专业银行——则不断升级既有服务并将其迁移至应用端。
尽管两类机构在所有权和运营架构方面存在差异，但竞争重点高度一致：便利性、信任度和日常客户互动。
尽管银行业务加速向移动端迁移，传统银行巨头仍主导网站流量
银行类网站流量仍具有明显的本地化特征，主要市场排名靠前的位置大多由本土金融机构占据。Chase、CommBank、SMBC、HDFC Bank、DBS 和 BCA 等传统银行凭借较高的品牌认知度、丰富的产品体系以及长期积累的客户关系，持续保持网站流量优势。不过，新型数字银行品牌也已跻身部分市场前列，其中最具代表性的包括韩国的 Toss、菲律宾的 Maya 和日本的 Rakuten Bank。这表明，新兴参与者若能建立强大的本地市场影响力并提供差异化数字服务，同样可以取得网站流量领先地位。
新型银行 借助移动端拓展市场，传统银行保持规模优势
2026 年上半年，Nubank 仍是全球下载量最高的核心银行类应用，其后依次为 Revolut 和 MariBank / SeaBank。多款数字银行和新型银行应用跻身下载量前列，反映出拉丁美洲、欧洲和东南亚市场对移动端银行服务的普及程度较高。YONO SBI、HDFC、Santander、CAIXA Tem 和 CAIXA 等传统银行应用也保持了可观规模，表明传统银行在本土市场仍拥有庞大的移动端用户群。
数字化挑战者与传统银行均实现了下载量增长。CAIXA Tem 以 53.5% 的增幅位居首位，MariBank / SeaBank、easypaisa、Banco PicPay、CAIXA 和 YONO SBI 也取得强劲增长。GoTyme Bank South Africa、Hana OneQ 和 Nueva BNA+ 等新上榜应用表明，焕新的产品定位和不断扩展的数字银行服务能够迅速赢得市场。增长机会并非新型银行专属，持续升级移动端体验的传统银行同样可以实现增长。
新型银行着力构建信任，传统银行重塑数字化体验
新型银行正逐步破解其普及过程中的一大障碍——消费者信任。Chime 和 Nubank 等品牌着重强化安全控制、实时提醒、快速响应的客户支持及人工服务，让用户相信，数字优先型银行同样能够提供传统成熟机构所具备的可靠性与安全保障。
与此同时，传统银行正通过升级移动端体验作出回应。Kotak 811 和 Hana OneQ 等重新推出的应用更加注重简洁界面、整合式账户视图、便捷导航及更具吸引力的功能。通过将长期积累的品牌信誉与新型银行的设计理念和易用性相结合，传统银行既能增强数字端用户参与度，也能保持对移动优先挑战者的竞争力。
